body:
Adds `FFT2D5MODEL="ORIGINAL"`, prints the selected model, and rejects its use with other solver types. ORIGINAL remains the default and only supported mainline model. Field calculations are unchanged.

Validation: configuration unit tests pass with 1 and 4 OpenMP threads.

**Test case:** cold protons (β=0.001), a 5 m uniform round bunch with transverse RMS 10 mm, ZeroSC or 10 pC. A uniform vertical magnetic field gives R=2 m. Track 10 m in 100 steps; compare RMS sizes and emittances with committed 658, PyORBIT and the analytic ZeroSC radial reference.

**`FFT2D5MODEL` choices:**
- `"ORIGINAL"`: independent transverse 2D slices and a local longitudinal closure (`g=6.36` for `PIPEMODE=OPEN`). Default and only supported choice in this PR.
- `"FINITE_SOURCE"`: experimental local build only, outside this PR. Straight geometry uses a 3D finite-source solve; circular geometry uses curvature-corrected 2D slices plus a 1D arc integral. Its circular longitudinal closure remains local.

`PIPEMODE` is a separate longitudinal-model setting; it is not another `FFT2D5MODEL` choice.

**Agreement (100 steps):** local ORIGINAL and committed 658 agree closely. At 10 pC, final transverse RMS sizes agree with PyORBIT within 0.6%. Charged radial and vertical emittances differ by 12% and 50%; the maximum radial-size difference along the trajectory is 11%, so this is not a claim of converged agreement throughout.

**Analytic ZeroSC calculation:** exact circular trajectories in the uniform magnetic field give the mean-subtracted radial position–momentum covariance. Moments are integrated over the initial uniform disk, including its curved-volume Jacobian. OPALX samples at a common time; PyORBIT TEAPOT samples at a common lattice station. The plots show the corresponding separate analytic references. Endpoint radial-emittance errors are 0.028% for OPALX and 0.025% for PyORBIT; PyORBIT's maximum absolute curve error is 0.59% of the analytic peak. The apparent 15% endpoint difference came from mixing sampling conventions.

Plots are reference data from the local benchmark build, not PR-head tracking. No new solver physics is introduced by this PR.

![RMS comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/rms.png)

![Emittance comparison with common-time and common-station analytic ZeroSC references](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/emittance.png)

Artifacts are stored in [opalx-documents/examples/2026/2d5-1](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/tree/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1).

**100-step, 10 pC inputs:** [OPALX](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/opalx-10pc-100steps.in) · [PyORBIT](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/pyorbit-10pc-100steps.py). [Dependencies and provenance](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/readme.md); external particle and field-map assets are required.

Refs #658.
